q: The powerhouse of the cell is the
e: Mitochondria release energy from food during respiration.

q: Plants make food by
e: Plants make food by photosynthesis, using light, water and carbon dioxide.

q: The universal blood donor group is
e: Group O has no A or B antigens, so it is the universal donor.

q: The basic unit of heredity is the
e: A gene is the unit of inheritance.

q: Insulin is produced by the
e: The pancreas makes insulin, which controls blood sugar.

q: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin
e: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy.

q: The organ for gaseous exchange in humans is the
e: The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

q: Which blood cells fight infection?
e: White blood cells defend the body against infection.

q: The green pigment in plants is
e: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that traps light.

q: Malaria is caused by a
e: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan.

q: The vector of malaria is the female
e: The female Anopheles mosquito spreads malaria.

q: Which part of the cell controls its activities?
e: The nucleus controls the cell's activities.

q: The basic unit of life is the
e: All living things are made of cells.

q: Proteins are made in the
e: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

q: Chlorophyll is found in the
e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

q: The movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane is
e: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a semi-permeable membrane.

q: The loss of water vapour from plant leaves is called
e: Transpiration happens mainly through stomata.

q: Enzymes are
e: Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells.

q: Lack of vitamin C causes
e: Scurvy results from vitamin C deficiency.

q: Rickets is caused by a lack of
e: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium for strong bones.

q: Kwashiorkor is caused by a lack of
e: Kwashiorkor is a protein deficiency disease.

q: Haemoglobin in red blood cells carries
e: Haemoglobin binds oxygen for transport around the body.

q: Gaseous exchange in mammals takes place in the
e: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the alveoli.

q: The main nitrogenous waste of humans is
e: Urea is made in the liver and removed by the kidneys.

q: Bile is produced by the
e: The liver makes bile; the gall bladder only stores it.

q: The hormone that lowers blood sugar is
e: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood glucose.

q: Gregor Mendel did his experiments on
e: Mendel studied inheritance in garden pea plants.

q: A cross between two heterozygous tall plants (Tt × Tt) gives tall to short in the ratio
e: TT, Tt, Tt are tall and tt is short, giving 3 : 1.

q: A normal human body cell has how many chromosomes?
e: Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in body cells.

q: Gametes are produced by
e: Meiosis halves the chromosome number to make gametes.

q: Every food chain begins with
e: Producers (green plants) make food by photosynthesis.

q: Fungi that feed on dead organic matter are called
e: Saprophytes feed on dead and decaying matter.

q: A relationship in which both organisms benefit is
e: Mutualism benefits both partners.

q: Malaria is transmitted by the
e: The female Anopheles mosquito carries the Plasmodium parasite.

q: Sleeping sickness is spread by the
e: The tsetse fly transmits the trypanosome parasite.

q: The fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete is called
e: Fertilisation forms a zygote.

q: After fertilisation, the ovary of a flower develops into the
e: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovules become seeds.

q: Seeds with wing-like structures are mainly dispersed by
e: Wings help seeds drift on the wind.

q: Seeds need which conditions to germinate?
o: water, oxygen and a suitable temperature
e: Germination needs water, oxygen and a suitable temperature.

q: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from
e: Light splits water molecules, releasing oxygen.

q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly concerned with
o: packaging and secretion of cell products
e: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and secretes substances made in the cell.

q: Which of the following organisms is prokaryotic?
e: Bacteria such as E. coli lack a membrane-bound nucleus.

q: Which of these organisms belongs to the kingdom Fungi?
e: Mucor (bread mould) is a fungus; the others are algae or protozoans.

q: An arthropod with three pairs of legs and a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen belongs to the class
e: Insects have six legs and three body regions.

q: Salivary amylase begins the digestion of
e: Salivary amylase breaks starch down to maltose in the mouth.

q: Most absorption of digested food in humans occurs in the
e: The ileum has villi that give a large surface area for absorption.

q: The xylem vessels of a plant mainly transport
e: Xylem carries water and dissolved mineral salts from roots to leaves.

q: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the
e: The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood to the left atrium.

q: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
e: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the
e: Each nephron filters blood and forms urine.

q: The hormone that regulates water reabsorption in the kidney tubules is
e: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) increases water reabsorption in the kidney.

q: In a reflex arc, the impulse passes from the sensory neurone to the
e: The sequence is receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector.

q: The part of the brain that coordinates balance and body movement is the
e: The cerebellum controls balance, posture and muscular coordination.

q: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria living in the root nodules of legumes belong to the genus
e: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in legume root nodules.

q: Which Nigerian vegetation zone is characterised by plants with stilt (prop) roots?
e: Mangroves of the coastal swamps have stilt roots and pneumatophores.

q: About what percentage of energy is passed from one trophic level to the next in a food chain?
e: Only about 10% of energy is transferred; the rest is lost as heat and waste.

q: A heterozygous tall plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt). The ratio of tall to short offspring is
e: Tt × tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers, so 1 : 1.

q: A carrier woman (XHXh) marries a normal man (XHY). What fraction of all their children is expected to be haemophiliac sons?
e: Offspring are XHXH, XHXh, XHY and XhY in equal numbers, so 1/4 are haemophiliac sons.

q: In a dihybrid cross between two double heterozygotes (AaBb × AaBb) producing 160 offspring, how many are expected to be double recessive (aabb)?
e: The double recessive class is 1/16 of 160 = 10.

q: Two parents are both carriers of sickle cell (AS × AS). Out of 200 children, how many are expected to have sickle cell anaemia (SS)?
e: One quarter of the children are SS, and 1/4 of 200 = 50.

q: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. Their children can only be of group
e: IAIB × ii gives IAi (A) and IBi (B) only.

q: The theory that characters acquired during an organism's lifetime can be inherited was proposed by
e: Lamarck proposed the inheritance of acquired characters.

q: Parallel venation in leaves is typical of
e: Monocot leaves such as maize and grass have parallel veins.

q: The plant hormone responsible for phototropism is
e: Unequal distribution of auxin makes shoots bend towards light.

q: The main function of the placenta in a pregnant woman is to
o: exchange materials between mother and foetus
e: The placenta passes oxygen and nutrients to the foetus and removes its wastes.

q: The hormone that maintains the uterine lining during pregnancy is
e: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterine wall and pregnancy.

q: Which of the following is an excretory product of plants?
e: Latex, resins, gums and tannins are plant excretory products.

q: Which reagent is used to test for protein in a food sample?
e: Biuret reagent turns violet or purple in the presence of protein.

q: Which of the following is an abiotic factor in an ecosystem?
e: Light intensity is a non-living (abiotic) factor.

q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
e: Poliomyelitis is caused by the polio virus; the others are bacterial.
